explanations: The PATCH handler copies every EDITABLE field from the body into `changes`, including fields the client did not send, which become `undefined`. Spreading `{ ...current, ...changes }` then overwrites the stored values with undefined, so a PATCH that only moves `startsAt` wipes `reason`, `notes` and `durationMinutes`. PATCH must only apply fields present in the request (e.g. check `field in body`).

The first PATCH saves version 4. The second compares its If-Match "3" to `"${current.version}"` = "4" and returns 412. 409 is only used for cancelled/completed status; there is no lock state; the ETag comparison is a plain string match, so strong ETags work.

The handler checks `current.status === "cancelled"` first and returns 200 with the existing record without bumping the version, so the retry is harmless. The 409 branch is only reached for checked_in/completed; nothing filters cancelled rows from `get`; no new resource is created.

PATCH rejects any field outside EDITABLE, and `status` is not listed, so state transitions go through a dedicated action endpoint that enforces 'booked -> cancelled' and treats repeats as no-ops. Express handles PATCH bodies fine, PATCH does return an ETag here, and cancellation keeps the same id.
